hints.title: Condition Monotonicity
hints.text: If substring s[left..right] contains a character with frequency at least k, any extension ending at right..n - 1 also satisfies the condition.

hints.title: Two-Pointer Sliding Window
hints.text: Expand right and increment frequency count. While the frequency of the current character reaches at least k, add n - right to the total and increment left.

hints.title: Linear Accumulation
hints.text: Both left and right pointers advance monotonically from 0 to n in O(n) total operations.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def numberOfSubstrings(self, s: str, k: int) -> int:
        from collections import Counter
        counts = Counter()
        left = 0
        ans = 0
        n = len(s)
        
        for right in range(n):
            counts[s[right]] += 1
            while counts[s[right]] >= k:
                ans += n - right
                counts[s[left]] -= 1
                left += 1
                
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Each character is processed at most twice (once by right, once by left) with 26-character frequency arrays.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: O(n^2) substring inspection is unnecessarily slow.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1) memory using fixed 26-size counter array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applies standard dynamic sliding window with suffix extension counting.
